transcript.en: Good morning everyone.
transcript.zh: 大家早上好。

transcript.en: In today's seminar, Grant Freeman, a biologist who specializes in identifying insects, and who works for the Australian Quarantine Service, has come to talk to us about his current research work.
transcript.zh: 在今天的讲座中，澳大利亚检疫中心专门鉴定昆虫的生物学家，格兰特·弗里曼与我们讲讲他目前的调查工作。

transcript.en: Right, well, over to you, Grant.
transcript.zh: 好的，交给你了，格兰特。

transcript.en: Good morning, everyone.
transcript.zh: 大家早上好。

transcript.en: I'm sure that you know that the quarantine service regulates all food brought into Australia.
transcript.zh: 想必你们知道检疫中心管理所有引入澳大利亚的食物。

transcript.en: Well, obviously they want to protect Australia from diseases that might come in with imported goods, but they also want to prevent insect pests from being introduced into the country, and that's where I have a part to play.
transcript.zh: 显然，他们要保护澳洲不受进口食物所带来的疾病侵扰，但是他们也要防止害虫被引入国内，而这就是我的工作。

transcript.en: Anyway, my current research involves trying to find a particular type of bee, the Asian Honey Bee, and finding out whether there are any of them around in various states of Australia.
transcript.zh: 总之，我目前的工作就是找到一种特殊的蜂，亚洲蜜蜂，看看它们是否存在于澳大利亚的各州。

transcript.en: We discovered a few of them in Queensland once and eradicated them.
transcript.zh: 我们发现昆士兰有一些便把它们消灭了

transcript.en: Now, we're pretty keen to make sure that there aren't any more getting in, particularly to New South Wales and other states.
transcript.zh: 现在，我们很想确定它们没有更多的进入国内，特别是新南威尔士州和其他州。

transcript.en: What's wrong with Asian Honey Bees?
transcript.zh: 亚洲蜜蜂有什么问题吗

transcript.en: Are they so different from Australian bees?
transcript.zh: 它们和澳洲蜜蜂不同吗

transcript.en: Well, in fact, they look almost the same, but they are infested with mites - microscopic creatures which live on them, and which can seriously damage our own home-grown bees, or could even wipe them out.
transcript.zh: 事实上，它们看起来几乎一样，但它们都有螨虫——一种生活在它们身上的微小生物，这些螨虫会严重损害我们自己的本土蜜蜂，甚至可能使它们灭绝。

transcript.en: Well, what would happen if Australian bees died out?
transcript.zh: 如果澳洲蜂灭绝了会发生什么？

transcript.en: Well, the honey from Australian bees is of excellent quality, much better than the stuff the Asian bees produce.
transcript.zh: 澳洲蜂的蜜质量很高，它比亚洲蜂产出的蜜好很多。

transcript.en: In fact, Australia exports native Queen bees to a large number of countries because of this.
transcript.zh: 事实上，正因为这点，澳大利亚出口大量的蜂王到各个国家。

transcript.en: When the European Honey Bee was first discovered out in the bush, we found they made really unpleasant honey and they were also too big to pollinate many of our native flowers here in Australia.
transcript.zh: 当欧洲蜜蜂第一次在灌木丛中发现时，我们发现它们产出的蜂蜜很不好，并且它们太大了，无法对澳洲的许多花授粉。

transcript.en: That must have had a devastating effect on the natural flora.
transcript.zh: 这对自然界的植物肯定有毁灭性的影响。

transcript.en: Did you lose any species?
transcript.zh: 你们失去了一些物种吗？

transcript.en: No, we managed to get them under control before that happened but if Asian bees got in there could be other consequences.
transcript.zh: 没有，我们设法在那种情况发生前控制它们，但是如果亚洲蜂进入国内将会发生另一种后果。

transcript.en: We could lose a lot of money because you might not be aware, but it's estimated that native bees pollination of flower and vegetable crops is worth 1.2 billion dollars a year.
transcript.zh: 你可能不会意识到我们会因此失去很多钱，但是据估计本土蜜蜂对花和蔬菜的授粉每年价值12亿美元。

transcript.en: So in a way they're the farmer's friend. Oh, and another thing is, if you're stung by an Asian Honey Bee, it can produce an allergic reaction in some people; so they're much more dangerous than native bees.
transcript.zh: 所以它们是农民的朋友。另一方面，如果你被亚洲蜜蜂咬了，有些人会发生过敏反应，所以它们比本土蜜蜂更危险。

transcript.en: How will you know if Asian bees have entered Australia?
transcript.zh: 你怎么知道是否亚洲蜂进入澳洲了？

transcript.en: We're looking at the diet of the bird called the Rainbow Bee Eater.
transcript.zh: 我们观看一种鸟的饮食，它们叫做彩虹蜂虎。

transcript.en: The Bee Eater doesn't care what it eats, as long as they're insects.
transcript.zh: 只要是昆虫，它们不关心吃的是什么。

transcript.en: But the interesting thing about this bird is that we are able to analyse exactly what it eats and that's really helpful if we're looking for introduced insects.
transcript.zh: 但是关于这种鸟有趣的是我们可以分析出它吃的是什么，这对我们寻找引进的昆虫很有帮助。

transcript.en: How come?
transcript.zh: 为什么

transcript.en: Because insects have their skeletons outside their bodies, so the Bee Eaters digest the meat from the inside.
transcript.zh: 因为昆虫的体外有骨骼，所以鸟消化掉它们内部的肉，

transcript.en: Then they bring up all the indigestible bits of skeleton and, of course, the wings in a pellet - a small ball of waste material which they cough up.
transcript.zh: 然后它们吐出所有不消化的骨骼，由废料组成的小球里面会有翅膀。

transcript.en: That sounds a bit unpleasant.
transcript.zh: 听起来很不好受。

transcript.en: So, how do you go about it?
transcript.zh: 那么你们要怎么处理它。

transcript.en: In the field we track down the Bee Eaters and find their favourite feeding spots, you know, the places where the birds usually feed.
transcript.zh: 我们跟踪这些鸟，找到它们最喜欢的觅食点，也就是鸟类通常进食的地方。

transcript.en: It's here that we can find the pellets.
transcript.zh: 我们可以在这里找到那些小球

transcript.en: We collect them up and take them back to the laboratory to examine the contents.
transcript.zh: 我们收集好后，带回实验室研究其成份。

transcript.en: How do you do that?
transcript.zh: 你们会怎么做？

transcript.en: The pellets are really hard, especially if they have been out in the sun for a few days so, first of all, we treat them by adding water to moisten them and make them softer.
transcript.zh: 这些小球很硬，特别是在太阳底下烤了几天后。所以首先，我们加水使它们变湿、软化，

transcript.en: Then we pull them apart under the microscope.
transcript.zh: 然后将它们撕开放在显微镜底下

transcript.en: Everything's all scrunched up but we're looking for wings so we just pull them all out and straighten them.
transcript.zh: 所有东西都揉成一团，但是要找到翅膀，所以我们将它们挑出、弄平整。

transcript.en: Then we identify them to see if we can find any Asian bee wings.
transcript.zh: 然后我们看看能不能找到任何亚洲蜂的翅膀。

transcript.en: And how many have you found?
transcript.zh: 你们找到了多少

transcript.en: So far our research shows that Asian bees have not entered Australia in any number - it's a good result and much more reliable than trying to find live ones as evidence of introduced insects.
transcript.zh: 到目前为止，研究表明亚洲蜂还没有进入澳洲，这个结果很好，这比找寻活着的蜜蜂作为证据要可靠的多。

transcript.en: Well, that's fascinating!
transcript.zh: 真不错。

transcript.en: Thank you, Grant, for those insights.
transcript.zh: 格兰特，谢谢你的这些见解，

transcript.en: I hope that you might inspire some of our students here to conduct some similar experiments.
transcript.zh: 我希望你能启发这里的一些学生做相似的实验。
